claim: Latent Diffusion (Rombach et al.) runs diffusion in the latent space of a pretrained autoencoder and introduces cross-attention layers to condition on general inputs such as text or bounding boxes, cutting compute versus pixel-space DMs.
quote: we apply them in the latent space of powerful pretrained autoencoders... By introducing cross-attention layers into the model architecture, we turn diffusion models into powerful and flexible generators for general conditioning inputs such as text or bounding boxes... significantly reducing computational requirements compared to pixel-based DMs

claim: Dhariwal & Nichol's classifier guidance uses gradients from a classifier trained on noisy images to steer sampling, with a single scale hyperparameter trading diversity for fidelity (equivalent to sampling from p(y|x)^s).
quote: scaling the gradients beyond 1.0 smoothly trades off recall (a measure of diversity) for higher precision and IS (measures of fidelity)... a single hyperparameter, the scale of the classifier gradients, can be tuned to trade off diversity for fidelity

claim: Ho & Salimans' classifier-free guidance jointly trains a conditional and an unconditional diffusion model and combines their score estimates, achieving the quality/diversity trade-off of classifier guidance without any classifier.
quote: guidance can be indeed performed by a pure generative model without such a classifier... we jointly train a conditional and an unconditional diffusion model, and we combine the resulting conditional and unconditional score estimates

claim: DiT (Peebles & Xie) replaces the U-Net with a transformer over latent patches and conditions via adaLN-Zero, regressing scale/shift (and a zero-initialized dimension-wise scale) from the sum of t and c embeddings, beating cross-attention and in-context conditioning on FID while most compute-efficient.
quote: regress[es them] from the sum of the embedding vectors of t and c... adaLN-Zero block yields lower FID than both cross-attention and in-context conditioning while being the most compute-efficient... replacing the commonly-used U-Net backbone with a transformer that operates on latent patches

claim: In HuggingFace diffusers, the guidance_scale parameter controls how strongly the text prompt influences generation; higher values follow the prompt more closely but too high introduces artifacts.
quote: The `guidance_scale` parameter affects how much the prompt influences image generation... Higher `guidance_scale` values push the model to follow the prompt more closely, and if this value is too high, you may observe some artifacts in the generated image.

claim: Imagen shows generic large frozen language models like T5 are effective text encoders for image synthesis, and scaling the text encoder boosts fidelity and image-text alignment more than scaling the diffusion model itself.
quote: generic large language models (e.g. T5), pretrained on text-only corpora, are surprisingly effective at encoding text for image synthesis... increasing the size of the language model in Imagen boosts both sample fidelity and image-text alignment much more than increasing the size of the image diffusion model

claim: Stable Diffusion 3 Medium is a Multimodal Diffusion Transformer (MMDiT) using three fixed pretrained text encoders (OpenCLIP-ViT/G, CLIP-ViT/L, and T5-xxl) to process prompts before diffusion.
quote: Stable Diffusion 3 Medium is a Multimodal Diffusion Transformer (MMDiT) text-to-image generative model... uses three fixed, pretrained text encoders: OpenCLIP-ViT/G... CLIP-ViT/L... T5-xxl

claim: The reference CompVis/latent-diffusion implementation (the original LDM codebase) has roughly 14.1k GitHub stars.
